name: Virtual Galaxy Infotech Ltd
tagline: Nagpur-based BFSI IT-product company (core-banking platform 'e-Banker' for cooperative / RRB / urban co-op banks, plus ERP and e-governance) - FY26 revenue Rs 182 Cr (+52%), PAT Rs 46 Cr (25% margin), EBITDA margin ~46%, ~42% recurring, order book 2x YoY to Rs 145.5 Cr, first international win (Botswana) - and trading at only ~10x TTM earnings
business_overview: Virtual Galaxy Infotech (26+ years operating, NSE SME IPO 2025) is a product-led BFSI software company. Core product e-Banker is a core-banking platform sold mainly to district central cooperative banks, regional rural banks and urban co-op banks; it also sells an ERP suite and e-governance solutions and does custom IT services. BFSI is ~90% of revenue, ERP ~9%, e-gov <1%. Sovrenn Discovery seed (2026-09-02, 'Excellent Results Jun-26' bucket). No dedicated ValuePickr thread - web/filings/concall-only read.

fundamentals_narrative: This is the most interesting risk/reward in the batch. Virtual Galaxy is an asset-light BFSI software-product company growing 50-60%, with a 46% EBITDA margin, 25% PAT margin, ~47% ROE and ~42% recurring revenue - and it trades at only ~10x TTM earnings. The order book doubled year-on-year, management has a dated Rs 500 Cr-by-FY29 revenue target (~40% CAGR from Rs 182 Cr), and the first international wins (Botswana, Zimbabwe) show the product travels. The pre-listing history is lumpier than the FY25-26 story suggests, though: revenue grew slowly in FY24 (+~6% to Rs 63.5 Cr) even as PAT margin jumped abruptly from ~3% (FY22/23) to ~26.5% - a step-change screener.in flags as possibly including capitalised interest, not a clean read. FY25 and now FY26 (46.2% EBITDA margin) have repeated the high-margin result, which argues the FY24 jump was a real structural shift rather than a one-off, but two years of confirmation is not the same as an audited long-run pattern. Debtor days, which had risen (94->146 days per screener's FY24 cut), improved sharply to ~65 days by FY26 per the company's own disclosure - easing the co-op-bank receivables worry. Client concentration in small, slow-paying cooperative and government-linked banks, the competitive set (Infrasoft, Intellect, TCS BaNCS, Nelito), and the usual NSE SME constraints - thin liquidity, ~1-year listed history, no analyst or forum scrutiny, eventual main-board migration - remain the open risks.
technical_read: Not pulled. NSE SME; up since the 2025 listing.

bear_case: FY24 PAT margin jumped abruptly from ~3% (FY22/FY23) to ~26.5% in a single year while revenue growth was slow (+~6%) that year - screener.in flags possible capitalised interest; FY25/FY26 repeating the high margin argues it's structural but pre-dates full audited scrutiny

Client concentration in small district-cooperative / RRB / urban co-op banks and government counterparties - slow payment, receivables risk (debtor days did improve to ~65 in FY26 from a worse ~146 read in FY24, easing this)
Competitive core-banking segment (Infrasoft, Intellect, TCS BaNCS, Nelito) - switching is sticky but new-bank wins are contested
NSE SME: ~1-year listed history, thin liquidity, no analyst/forum scrutiny, eventual main-board migration overhang
Guidance credibility is still being established - only ~1 year of public quarterly results exist to judge management's promise-vs-delivery record

verdict_headline: Asset-light BFSI software-product company growing 50-60% at a 46% EBITDA margin and ~47% ROE, ~42% recurring, order book 2x YoY, a dated Rs 500 Cr-by-FY29 target - and only ~10x TTM earnings. Deep-dive pass 1: the FY24 margin step-up has now repeated for two more years (FY25, FY26) and debtor days have improved, not worsened. thesis_fit 10x-in-2-3-years, conviction Medium-High.
verdict_reasoning: Sovrenn Discovery seed; the datapoints (Q1 FY27 revenue +60%, order book Rs 145.5 Cr, FY26 revenue Rs 182 Cr / PAT Rs 46 Cr) hold up against the actual results and concall

Deep-dive pass 1 (multi-year read): revenue was Rs 43 Cr (FY22) -> Rs 60 Cr (FY23, +38%) -> Rs 63.5 Cr (FY24, +6%, slow) -> roughly doubled (FY25) -> Rs 182 Cr (FY26, +52%). PAT margin was ~3% through FY22/23, then jumped to ~26.5% in FY24 and has held ~25-27% since. A single-year margin jump would be a real red flag; two further years (FY25, FY26) repeating it, plus Q1 FY27 delivering +60% against 40-50% guidance, argue it is a structural re-rating in the business (asset-light SaaS/AMC mix, operating leverage) rather than a one-off - though the FY24 jump itself pre-dates the IPO and independent scrutiny, so it is a monitored assumption, not a proven one
Debtor days actually improved from a concerning ~146 (screener's FY24 cut) to ~65 by FY26 per company disclosure - the receivables-risk bear point from the initial write-up is easing, not worsening

Thesis fit: four_box score 4.0 (tailwind/tam/moat/valuation all yes) supports 10x-in-2-3-years. At ~10x TTM earnings against 40-60% delivered/guided growth, the reverse-P/E implies the market is pricing close to flat growth - a clear underestimated setup if the FY25/26 margin and growth pattern holds for one more year

Conviction Medium -> Medium-High: two consecutive audited-adjacent years (FY25, FY26) of high-margin, high-growth performance, a doubled order book, and guidance being delivered (not just given) push this past Medium. Kept below High because of the FY24 margin-jump's unresolved capitalised-interest question, guidance credibility being judged on only ~1 year of public quarters, and continued SME-exchange thin liquidity / zero independent (analyst or VP-forum) scrutiny
Live-theme match: priority-2 'US + Indian software / product-SaaS turn' - a genuine Indian vertical-software product company with above-index growth

revisit_after_30d unchanged (rule sets floor only off trusted-conviction-floor, not deep-dive conviction) - but this name should stay on the light-guidance/short revisit cadence to watch whether the FY26 margin and debtor-day improvement holds through FY27

growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: At ~10x TTM earnings the multiple implies almost no growth; delivered and guided growth is 40-60%, so the rate of change is far ahead of what the multiple prices - the classic re-rating setup, subject to margin and receivables holding.

four_box.note: Product-led BFSI core-banking software with international wins (Botswana/Zimbabwe) and sticky switching costs scores well on all four boxes; only ~10x TTM earnings against 50-60% growth and 46% EBITDA margin is explicitly cheap. The FY24 margin step-up (now repeated FY25/FY26) and SME-liquidity/scrutiny risk are separate open questions, not scored here.
